text:
marco_sales: BetaBank POC demo failed—client saw broken SSE payloads and an immediate close when the response contained embedded JSON with certificates info. Happened during a live demo. Need fast triage.

beta_demo_bot: (system) client_id: beta-001, req: req_9c8b, path: /v1/generate/stream, env: dedicated-poc, region: eu-west-1

nina_se: Any raw frames from the client? curious if termination includes TLS alerts or just TCP RST.

beta_demo_bot: client capture (sanitized): ```
data: {"part":1,"msg":"Credentials: {\"cert\":\"-----BEGIN CERT"}

data: {"part":2,"msg":"-----END CERT-----\", "done":true}
```

oli_runtime: The first event looks cut right after the BEGIN CERT line. Our runtime logs show a FIN from client 192.0.2.45 immediately after sending that chunk. No ECONNRESET recorded on our side. Suggests client or middlebox closed connection.

fae_support: BetaBank mentioned a DLP proxy that inspects HTTPS and does TLS interception. Those appliances sometimes drop streams when they detect suspicious payloads like long cert blocks.

marco_sales: They also asked about enterprise compliance / security questionnaire answers earlier—could the DLP be inline and mutating responses?

nina_se: Yes, TLS MITM devices terminate TLS and re-encrypt. They may have rules to truncate or rewrite bodies that match patterns (like PEM blocks). If the proxy stops streaming mid-chunk the SSE event won't terminate and the client sees a trailing partial JSON.

oli_runtime: Quick reproducer: ask Beta devs to curl the endpoint from inside their network with verbose output: `curl -v -N "https://poc.beta-bank.example/v1/generate/stream?req=req_9c8b"` and capture bytes. If curl shows truncation we can blame the appliance.

fae_support: Also ask them to check their DLP logs for rule hits around req_9c8b timestamp. We saw similar with BankCorp last quarter; DLP flagged PEM blocks and dropped the connection to scan.

marco_sales: If it's the DLP, what's our recommended quick fix for the demo?

nina_se: Two options: 1) Bypass the DLP for the demo origin (allowlist) or 2) instruct the server to avoid embedding raw certificate PEMs in streamed JSON; instead redact or send a URL-safe base64 or short fingerprint that the client can fetch over a separate TLS call. For POC speed allowlist is faster.

oli_runtime: Server-side mitigation: wrap sensitive payloads in an `event: meta` with `data: <base64>` and ensure chunk sizes < 8KB so intermediate devices are less likely to trigger rules. Also add keepalive comments every 10s to avoid idle timeouts: `: ka\n\n`.

fae_support: From compliance side, record the change in the SOC questionnaire answer: when asked about egress interception, note that some enterprise customers have TLS-inspection devices and we recommend allowlisting or using secure artifact hosting. We'll update the POC checklist.

beta_demo_bot: Customer says they can test an allowlist for 30 minutes. They will revert rules during the demo window.

marco_sales: Great. Can we also confirm whether our hosted runtime can redact cert-like patterns automatically? Customer worried about leaking certs.

nina_se: We don't auto-redact by default; but we can enable a lightweight canary transform that scans outgoing events for PEM headers and replaces bodies with a `[REDACTED_CERT]` token for POC environments. I can push a canary flag to the dedicated pool for BetaBank with `X-REDACT-CERTS: true`.

oli_runtime: I'll deploy the canary now and add `X-KA: true` and `X-REDACT-CERTS: true` headers to responses. ETA 12m. I'll post the canary URL when live.

fae_support: Also remind the customer to capture their DLP hit logs and the timestamp so we can correlate with `req_9c8b`. That helps security review.

marco_sales: Excellent. Any client-side tips to avoid crash if partial frame arrives? They use a JavaScript SPA with EventSource.

nina_se: Client robust parser: buffer `data:` lines until a blank line, then attempt JSON.parse. If parse fails, keep buffering up to a size threshold, then discard and log. Example: ```
let buf='';
source.onmessage = e => { buf += e.data; try{ const o=JSON.parse(buf); buf=''; handle(o); }catch(e){ if(buf.length>65536){ console.error('drop partial'); buf=''; } } };
```
This prevents UI crashes.

marco_sales: Thanks everyone. I'll tell BetaBank to try the allowlist and wait for the canary. I'll also add a note to the RFP/security thread about potential TLS-inspection impacts on streaming. :white_check_mark:
